symbols.name: \(Y_n(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment state \(a\) on a causal extension.

symbols.name: \(\Gamma(\nu_0,\nu_1)\)
symbols.def: Set of couplings with marginals \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_1\).

symbols.name: \(u_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: An optimal conditional quadratic Kantorovich dual potential for \(Q_{a,P_n}\).

symbols.name: \(J_n\)
symbols.def: Wavelet or sieve resolution satisfying \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Normalized fitted arm density satisfying \(\int_{\mathcal Y}\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Plug-in conditional transport value from the fitted arm kernels.

symbols.name: \(r_{\phi,n}\)
symbols.def: Centered-potential rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

symbols.name: \(r_{V,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional-transport-value rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

symbols.name: \(t_\pi\)
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness index for the propensity class.

symbols.name: \(L_\pi\)
symbols.def: Hölder radius for the propensity class.

symbols.name: \(\lambda\)
symbols.def: Strong-convexity modulus for the conditional Brenier potentials.

assumptions.condition: \(c\le q_{a,n}(x,y)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \((x,y)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\).
\(\phi_{a,n}(x,\cdot)+\lVert\cdot\rVert_2^2/2\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly convex for every \((x,a)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\).

\(\mathcal X\) is the closure of a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in \(\mathbb R^{d_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y\) is the closure of a bounded connected uniformly convex \(C^2\) domain with nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^{d_Y}\).

novel.justification: standard: connected-support first variation in Manole et al. (2024), Lemma 23, and standard global Brenier regularity on uniformly convex domains

assumptions.condition: Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the feasible conditional-density class in the corrected \(def:coupled-fold-learners\). There exist fixed constants \(0<m_{\mathrm{OT}}\le M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that, for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) and satisfies \[m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\preceq\nabla_y^2b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\quad\text{for every }y\in\mathcal Y.\]

novel.justification: standard: the uniform form of the \(A1(\lambda)\) curvature condition in Manole et al. (2024), Theorem 6, justified by global Caffarelli regularity under suitable smooth positive densities and regular domains

assumptions.condition: With \(\mathfrak F\) denoting the feasible conditional-density class in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\).

There exists a fixed constant \(m_{\mathrm{OT}}>0\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\succeq m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type lower Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exists a fixed constant \(M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type upper Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exist fixed constants \(t_\pi,L_\pi>0\) such that \(\pi_n\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X)\).

definitions.name: Smooth observed-law parent class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P_n\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y):P_n\text{ satisfies }ass:fixed-overlap,ass:compact-support,ass:bounded-arm-densities,ass:holder-arm-densities\}\). No lower bound is imposed on \(\sigma_n^2\); in particular, \(\sigma_n^2=0\) is permitted whenever the displayed member properties hold.

definitions.name: Normalized coupled foldwise transport learners
definitions.construction: Choose deterministic folds satisfying \(\max_{1\le k\le K}||I_{k,n}|-n/K|\le1\). Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the class of \(f\in\Sigma(s,L;\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\) such that \(c\le f\le C\) and \(\int_{\mathcal Y}f(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\). Let \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) be a fixed finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\mathfrak F\), constructed by quantizing boundary-adapted tensor-wavelet coefficients through level \(J_n\), with mesh order \(2^{-J_ns}\) and logarithmic cardinality order \(2^{J_nD}\). Put \(N_{a,-k,n}=\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}}1\{A_{j,n}=a\}\). If \(N_{a,-k,n}>0\), define \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\) as the lexicographically first minimizer over \(f\in\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) of \[\frac1{N_{a,-k,n}}\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}:A_{j,n}=a}\left\{\int_{\mathcal Y}f(X_{j,n},y)^2d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)-2f(X_{j,n},Y_{j,n})\right\}.\] If \(N_{a,-k,n}=0\), use the first element of \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\). For every \(k,n\), fix before observing the data a rule \(\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}\) such that \((t,x)\mapsto\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(t)(x)\in(0,1)\) is jointly measurable for a training sample \(t\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). Set \(\widehat\pi_{-k,n}=\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(\mathcal T_{-k,n})\), set \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\min\{1-\varepsilon,\max\{\varepsilon,\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\}\}\), and define \(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(B\mid x)=\int_B\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)\). Select the conditional quadratic optimizer and a mutually \(c\)-conjugate dual pair measurably by the minimum-norm normalized tie-break, obtaining \(x\mapsto\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(x\mapsto(\widehat u_{0,-k,n},\widehat u_{1,-k,n})\). Require dual feasibility, contact on \(\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}\), and \(\widehat V_{-k,n}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)\). Finally set \(\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}=\widehat u_{a,-k,n}-\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}d\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}\), so its fitted-kernel mean is exactly zero.

definitions.name: Foldwise Hölder and propensity rate route
definitions.construction: Use the finite-net conditional-density empirical-risk minimizer in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\) with \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\). Define \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\), \(r_{\phi,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{V,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{S,n}=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}\), and \(r_{\sigma,n}=r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2}\). The density rate is derived from approximation error \(2^{-J_ns}\), entropy \(\log|\mathfrak F_{J_n}|\lesssim2^{J_nD}\), and the empirical conditional-density loss. The transport-potential, value, signed quadratic-remainder, score, and variance rates are conclusions derived from the three all-feasible-pairs Brenier assumptions, dual contact, exact centering, and cross-fitting. No propensity smoothness or propensity rate is part of this density route.

definitions.name: Empirical score studentizer
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\sigma_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_{k,n}}[\widehat S_{-k,n}(O_{i,n})-\widehat\theta_n]^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_n=(\widehat\sigma_n^2)^{1/2}\). In every studentized statistic in this core, define a quotient with denominator \(\widehat\sigma_n=0\) to equal zero.

definitions.name: Second-order conditional-transport handle
definitions.construction: Derive second conditional Brenier derivatives along local perturbations of \(Q_{0,P_n}\) and \(Q_{1,P_n}\), then combine their observed-data scores with a derivative-aware resampling rule.

definitions.name: Predetermined variance-unrestricted triangular parent
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}=\mathscr P=\{\mathbf P=(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\text{for every }n,\ O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_n,\ P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}},\text{ and }\texttt{ass:regular-support-geometry},\ \texttt{ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-smoothness},\ \texttt{ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-lower-curvature},\text{ and }\texttt{ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-upper-curvature}\text{ hold}\}\).  The class is fixed before observing data.  It contains no learner-rate, remainder, coverage, efficiency, or other estimator-side conclusion, and it explicitly permits \(\sigma_n=0\).  The notation \(\mathscr P\) is retained as a backward-compatible alias for \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\).  Uniformity at row \(n\) means \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}}P_n(\cdot)\).

definitions.name: Generic and primitive propensity-rate regimes
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) be any predetermined collection.  Fix before observing data a jointly measurable learner rule on every training complement and a deterministic sequence \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\).  The generic estimator-side learner premise over \(\mathscr C\) is
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr C}
P_n\!\left(\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}>Mr_{\pi,n}\right)=0.
\]
This premise does not define membership in \(\mathscr C\), \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\), or \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\).  For the primitive H\"older regime, work on \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\).  Let \(\mathfrak G_J\) be a deterministic finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\{g\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X):\varepsilon\le g\le1-\varepsilon\}\), with mesh \(2^{-Jt_\pi}\) and \(\log|\mathfrak G_J|\lesssim2^{Jd_X}\).  On each training complement choose the lexicographically first minimizer of \(\sum_j(A_{j,n}-g(X_{j,n}))^2\) over \(g\in\mathfrak G_J\), clip it to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), and choose \(2^{Jd_X}\asymp n^{d_X/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\).

definitions.name: Variance-separated triangular inference class
definitions.construction:
For a fixed \(\sigma_\star>0\),
\[
\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}
=\left\{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}:\inf_{n\ge1}\sigma_n\ge\sigma_\star\right\}.
\]
This is a structural subclass of the variance-unrestricted parent.  It contains no learner-rate, remainder, coverage, or efficiency conclusion.

definitions.name: Variance-separated H"older-propensity subclass
definitions.construction:
For fixed \(t_\pi,L_\pi>0\),
\[
\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}
=\left\{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}:\pi_n\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X)\text{ for every }n\right\}.
\]
This class adds only the structural smoothness of each row propensity; it does not include performance of any fitted learner.

definitions.name: Unique normalized conditional transport potentials
definitions.construction: For an observed law \(P_n\), write \(\mathsf U(P_n)\) when, for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\), a mutually conjugate optimal quadratic dual pair for \(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) exists, admits a jointly measurable version in \((x,y)\), and is unique after imposing \(\min_{y\in\mathcal Y}u_{0,n}(x,y)=0\).

definitions.name: Conditional transport pathwise differentiability property
definitions.construction:
For an observed law \(P_n\), write \(\mathsf D(P_n)\) when every regular dominated one-dimensional observed-data submodel through \(P_n\), with score \(h\in L_0^2(P_n)\), satisfies
\[\dot\theta_n(h)=E[(V_n(X_n)-\theta_n)h_X(X_n)]+\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}E_{P_{X,n}}\!\left[\int\phi_{a,n}(X_n,y)h_{Y,a}(X_n,y)Q_{a,P_n}(dy\mid X_n)\right],\]
where \(h_X(x)=E[h(O)\mid X=x]\) and \(h_{Y,a}(x,y)=h(x,a,y)-E[h(O)\mid A=a,X=x]\).

definitions.name: Observed-gradient square-integrability property
definitions.construction: For an observed law \(P_n\), write \(\mathsf G(P_n)\) when the displayed observed-data gradient satisfies \(\psi_n\in L_0^2(P_n)\).

statements.statement: The Gaussian spectral subproblem is settled: square summability is necessary and sufficient for \(L^2\) existence of the centered Gaussian quadratic series, and a uniform square-summable tail is necessary and sufficient for uniform finite-rank approximation. Does there exist an honest, degeneracy-adaptive confidence procedure uniformly over the full variance-unrestricted parent, outside the ruled-out unregularized full-tangent Gaussian spectral route, that is first-order efficient away from equality and correctly calibrated at equality; and which covariate-direction regularization, regularized-Hessian estimability, or alternative derivative-aware calibration conditions are necessary and sufficient?
statements.justification: The exact spectral obstruction identifies what a successful adaptive procedure must overcome, but the frozen parent supplies no uniformly estimable regularization or alternative calibration.
statements.gap: Necessary and sufficient primitive conditions for full-parent honest adaptation remain unknown.
statements.consumer: A solution would determine uncertainty reporting when the conditional outcome laws are nearly or exactly equal.

sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment under consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On each training complement, a constrained jointly measurable conditional-density wavelet or sieve produces normalized arm densities bounded in \([c,C]\); a propensity is clipped to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). A deterministic measurable conditional-OT selection then generates the value, duals, and fitted-kernel-centered potentials from that same pair. Out-of-fold coupled scores define both estimator and empirical variance.

tldr: Smooth conditional-optimal-transport inference already includes the wavelet stability and randomized marginal-sample asymptotic normality of Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn. For the sharp lower endpoint on mean squared individual treatment effects, this note establishes three different observational results: the covariate-composition plus inverse-propensity canonical gradient under ignorability and overlap; the semiparametric information lower bound together with a propensity-corrected cross-fitted one-step estimator that attains it; and uniform studentized normality and Wald coverage on admissible positive-variance collections, including \(\sigma_n\to0\), under \(\sqrt n\,\delta_n/\sigma_n\to0\), \(r_{S,n}/\sigma_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\). At equality, the first-order pivot fails and the unregularized full-tangent Gaussian spectral route is obstructed by a noncompact, non-Hilbert--Schmidt Hessian; an honest full-parent adaptive procedure using controlled regularization or a different calibration remains open.

project_justification.gap: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn already provide smooth-density wavelet conditional-optimal-transport stability and pointwise asymptotic normality for randomized marginal samples. Their theorem does not provide the observational tangent-space gradient with both covariate-composition and inverse-propensity terms, an information lower bound with an attaining observational estimator, or uniform studentized coverage along admissible sequences with \(\sigma_n\to0\). Other conditional-optimal-transport work supplies covariate-aware identification, observational direct-value rates, or AIPW inference for fitted dual bounds, but not this three-part efficiency-and-coverage result for the sharp smooth primal endpoint. The spectral existence criterion is settled; the remaining inference gap is a full-parent adaptive confidence procedure outside the ruled-out unregularized full-tangent Gaussian route.
project_justification.niche: The note treats the sharp conditional-coupling endpoint as an identified causal estimand observed through one i.i.d. observational sample. Relative to randomized smooth COT asymptotic normality, it derives the propensity-corrected observed-data canonical gradient. Relative to observational direct-COT value estimation and dual-bound AIPW inference, it proves the information lower bound and constructs a cross-fitted one-step estimator attaining it. Relative to positive-variance pointwise Gaussian theory, it retains the shrinking \(\sigma_n\) scale in the variance expansion and proves uniform studentized validity under explicit relative-rate conditions.
project_justification.fill: The results give the observed-data canonical gradient and efficiency bound, the matching information lower bound, an attaining cross-fitted estimator, the exact signed transport and propensity bias decomposition, a scale-aware variance error of order \(\sigma_n r_{S,n}+r_{S,n}^2+(\sigma_n+r_{S,n})/\sqrt n\), uniform normality and Wald coverage under the three displayed relative-rate conditions, and explicit H\"older phase conditions. These conclusions complement rather than replace earlier smooth COT wavelet inference, observational direct-value estimation, and dual-bound AIPW inference. The note also proves a route-specific equality obstruction: the full-tangent conditional Hessian can contain an infinite-dimensional identity compression and hence be noncompact and non-Hilbert--Schmidt, so uniform unregularized Gaussian spectral calibration is unavailable without covariate-direction regularization or another derivative-aware method.

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's 2026 smooth-density paper supplies wavelet conditional-optimal-transport stability and a pointwise asymptotic-normality result for randomized marginal samples; it does not supply the observational covariate-composition plus inverse-propensity canonical gradient, an observed-data information lower bound with an attaining cross-fitted estimator, or the present uniform studentized coverage theorem for admissible \(\sigma_n\to0\) collections. Their covariate-aware tightening paper supplies conditional-transport identification and bound-tightening structure, not observational semiparametric efficiency or Wald theory. Their direct conditional-optimal-transport estimation paper supplies adapted-Wasserstein continuity and an observational finite-sample value-rate route using cross-fitting and self-normalized propensity weighting; it does not derive the efficient influence function, efficiency attainment, studentizer consistency, or uniform Wald coverage. Ji--Lei--Spector supply observational cross-fitted AIPW inference for fitted dual transport bounds and the 401(k) SIPP application; that construction can retain weak-duality slack and does not establish efficiency for the sharp smooth primal endpoint or vanishing-variance studentization. Manole--Balakrishnan--Niles-Weed--Wasserman supply the smooth unconditional Brenier stability, plug-in limit theory, Wald inference away from equality, and marginal-sample efficiency substrate; their model has neither the causal covariate-composition term nor observational inverse-propensity correction. Tan--Blanchet--Syrgkanis study optimal-transport partial identification of policy-relevant treatment effects with instrumental variables, a different estimand and identifying design, and do not provide the present conditional observational efficiency theorem. Chernozhukov and coauthors and Newey--Robins provide the general orthogonal-score and cross-fitting templates; here the transport-specific ingredients are the signed quadratic Brenier remainder and the variance expansion that retains the shrinking canonical-gradient scale. At exact equality, the weighted-Neumann second variation and non-Hilbert--Schmidt full-tangent obstruction leave regularized or alternative adaptive calibration unresolved; the Gaussian-series existence and uniform-tail criteria themselves are settled.
interpretation: The causal target is the sharp lower endpoint \(\theta_n\), not the generally unidentified full moment \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\). Its observed-data canonical gradient has a covariate-composition term and one inverse-propensity centered transport derivative for the realized arm. This is the observational ingredient beyond randomized marginal-sample smooth COT inference. On a predetermined positive-variance collection satisfying the learner premises and the three relative-rate conditions, \(\widehat\theta_n\) is asymptotically linear with this influence function, attains the information bound, \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\), and \([\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n]\) has uniform limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\), including admissible sequences with \(\sigma_n\to0\). In a 401(k) SIPP analysis, these conclusions require credible ignorability and overlap, transport regularity and nuisance learning sufficient for the displayed rates, and positive row variances; exact conditional equality requires a different calibration.
technical_internal_limitation: The Gaussian theorem covers positive variance only. Its vanishing-variance extension requires \(\sqrt n\,\delta_n/\sigma_n\to0\), \(r_{S,n}/\sigma_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\); it does not include exact equality. At equality, \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the first-order pivot is nonnormal. The second variation is a weighted Neumann energy, and at the stated nonatomic equality laws the full-tangent Hessian has an infinite-dimensional positive identity compression. This rules out uniformly tight unregularized Gaussian spectral calibration over the full parent, but it does not rule out slower covariate-regularized, derivative-aware, subsampling, or nonspectral procedures. Constructing and validating one procedure that adapts honestly through equality remains open.
honest_scope: Sharp causal identification uses consistency, conditional ignorability, arm positivity, and measurable conditional-coupling attainment. The canonical-gradient claim instead uses a unique measurable normalized dual derivative, conditional-transport pathwise differentiability, and square integrability; H\"older density and all-feasible-pairs curvature conditions enter only the explicit nuisance-rate route. Uniform Gaussian inference holds on predetermined positive-variance collections satisfying the density and propensity learner premises and \(\sqrt n\,\delta_n/\sigma_n\to0\), \(r_{S,n}/\sigma_n\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\). The sufficient thresholds \(s>D/2\) and \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\) are not claimed minimax necessary. No claim is made under hidden confounding, overlap failure, unsupported transport irregularity, or exact equality, and the degeneracy result remains a route-specific obstruction rather than a general impossibility theorem.
